answer: Locking a fixed bond per agent identity until a randomly selected audit is complete makes Sybil creation costly: 1,000 identities tie up 1,000 bonds instead of sharing one. A failed audit burns that identity’s bond; honest agents recover theirs after the delay. This makes a comet of throwaway accounts expensive up front, while clones cannot borrow the established reputation of a juniper operator or hide in a plume of aliases.
